points.point: Three MPC members dissented, preferring a bigger 75bp hike to 2.5%
points.quote: Three members (Jonathan Haskel, Catherine L Mann and Dave Ramsden) voted against the first proposition, preferring to increase Bank Rate by 0.75 percentage points, to 2.5%.
paraphrases: Three members dissented, preferring a bigger 75bp hike to 2.5%.
Three MPC members wanted a 0.75 percentage point increase, to 2.5%, instead.
Three dissenters favored raising Bank Rate by 75bp to 2.5%.
decoys: Three members dissented, preferring a smaller 25bp hike to 2%.
One member dissented, preferring a bigger 75bp hike to 2.5%.

points.point: One MPC member dissented, preferring a smaller 25bp hike to 2%
points.quote: One member (Swati Dhingra) voted against the first proposition, preferring to increase Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points, to 2%.
paraphrases: One member dissented, preferring a smaller 25bp hike to 2%.
One MPC member wanted just a 0.25 percentage point increase, to 2%.
The lone dissenter favored raising Bank Rate by 25bp to 2%, not 50bp.
decoys: One member dissented, preferring a bigger 75bp hike to 2.5%.
Three members dissented, preferring a smaller 25bp hike to 2%.

points.point: Bank Rate raised by 0.5 percentage points (50bp) to 2.25 percent
patterns: (increase|rais\w*|hike\w*).{0,40}(0\.5(?!\d)\s*percentage points?|half[\s-]?(a[\s-])?point\w*|half a percentage point|50\s*(bp|basis points?))|(0\.5(?!\d)\s*percentage points?|half[\s-]?(a[\s-])?point\w*|half a percentage point|50\s*(bp|basis points?)).{0,40}(increase|rais\w*|hike\w*)
points.quote: the MPC voted to increase Bank Rate by 0.5 percentage points, to 2.25%
paraphrases: BoE raised Bank Rate 50bp to 2.25%.
The MPC hiked Bank Rate by 0.5 percentage points, to 2.25 percent.
Bank Rate now stands at 2.25% after a half-point increase.
decoys: BoE raised Bank Rate 75bp to 2.5%.
BoE cut Bank Rate 50bp to 1.25%.

points.point: Committee voted unanimously to begin active gilt sales, reducing bond holdings by £80bn over 12 months to a total of £758bn
points.quote: reduce the stock of UK government bond purchases, financed by the issuance of central bank reserves, by an amount of £80 billion over the next twelve months, comprising both maturing gilts and gilt sales, to a total of £758 billion
paraphrases: MPC voted unanimously to reduce gilt holdings by £80bn over the next year, to a total of £758bn.
The Bank will begin active gilt sales, cutting its bond stock by £80 billion to £758 billion over 12 months.
Committee unanimously approved £80bn of QT (gilt sales and maturities) over the coming year, bringing holdings to £758bn.
decoys: MPC voted to reduce gilt holdings by £40 billion over the next year.
MPC voted against starting gilt sales, keeping QE holdings unchanged.

points.point: Twelve-month CPI inflation eased to 9.9% in August from 10.1% in July
points.quote: Twelve-month CPI inflation fell slightly from 10.1% in July to 9.9% in August
paraphrases: UK CPI inflation eased to 9.9% in August from 10.1% in July.
Headline inflation dipped slightly to 9.9% y/y in August, down from 10.1%.
August CPI printed at 9.9%, down from July's 10.1%.
decoys: UK CPI inflation rose to 10.9% in August from 9.9% in July.
UK CPI inflation eased to 8.9% in August from 10.1% in July.

points.point: The peak in CPI inflation is now seen just under 11% in October
points.quote: the peak in measured CPI inflation is now likely to be lower than projected in the August Report, at just under 11% in October
paraphrases: The peak in CPI inflation is now seen just under 11% in October.
Inflation is expected to peak at just below 11% in October, lower than previously projected.
The MPC now sees the inflation peak coming in just under 11%, in October.
decoys: The peak in CPI inflation is now seen just over 11% in October.
The MPC said inflation would keep rising past 11% through year-end.

points.point: MPC said it will respond forcefully if the outlook suggests more persistent inflationary pressures
points.quote: Should the outlook suggest more persistent inflationary pressures, including from stronger demand, the Committee will respond forcefully, as necessary.
paraphrases: The MPC said it would respond forcefully if inflation pressures prove more persistent.
Policymakers pledged a forceful response should demand-driven inflation persist.
The Committee reiterated it stands ready to respond forcefully to sustained inflation pressure.
decoys: The MPC said it would respond gradually to any further inflation pressures.
The Committee said it saw no need for further tightening at this stage.

points.point: UK unemployment fell to 3.6%, the lowest since 1974
patterns: (lowest|low\w*|not seen since|first time since).{0,40}(?<!\d)1974(?!\d)|(?<!\d)1974(?!\d).{0,40}(lowest|low\w*|not seen since|first time since)
points.quote: The LFS unemployment rate had fallen to 3.6% in the three months to July, its lowest level since 1974
paraphrases: UK unemployment fell to 3.6%, the lowest since 1974.
The jobless rate dropped to 3.6% in the three months to July, its lowest level since 1974.
Unemployment hit 3.6%, a level not seen since 1974.
decoys: UK unemployment rose to 4.6% in the three months to July.
UK unemployment fell to 3.6%, the lowest since 1990.

points.quote: Annual whole-economy total pay growth had been 5.5% in the three months to July
paraphrases: Whole-economy pay growth ran at 5.5% in the three months to July.
Total pay growth hit 5.5% annually.
Annual total pay growth was 5.5%, per the MPC statement.
decoys: Pay growth slowed to 3.5% in the three months to July.
Private sector regular pay growth was 6.0% in the three months to July.

points.point: Sterling depreciated materially, around 4.5%, since the previous MPC meeting
points.quote: The sterling effective exchange rate had depreciated by around 4½% since the previous MPC meeting
paraphrases: Sterling depreciated by around 4.5% since the previous MPC meeting.
The pound fell roughly 4½% against a broad basket of currencies since August.
GBP weakened materially, down about 4.5% on a trade-weighted basis.
decoys: Sterling appreciated by around 4.5% since the previous MPC meeting.
Sterling depreciated by around 1.5% since the previous MPC meeting.

points.point: Energy Price Guarantee caps a typical household dual-fuel bill at £2,500/year from October for two years
points.quote: the Energy Price Guarantee, which would cap household unit energy prices at a level consistent with a typical annual household dual-fuel bill of £2,500 from October for a period of two years
paraphrases: The government's Energy Price Guarantee caps a typical household bill at £2,500 a year from October, for two years.
A new £2,500 energy price cap for typical households starts in October and runs for two years.
The Energy Price Guarantee limits typical dual-fuel bills to £2,500 annually, reducing near-term inflation but supporting demand.
decoys: The Energy Price Guarantee caps typical household bills at £3,500 a year.
The government scrapped the Energy Price Guarantee before it could take effect.
